 Bring on 2027 – we'll see you on the sidelines!","url":"https://www.linkedin.com/posts/hutt-city-council_lower-hutts-scoring-big-were-excited-activity-7477475101920329728-2EbU"},{"@context":"http://schema.org","@type":"DiscussionForumPosting","author":{"@type":"Organization","name":"Hutt City Council","url":"https://nz.linkedin.com/company/hutt-city-council"},"datePublished":"2026-06-22T02:00:25.885Z","mainEntityOfPage":"https://www.linkedin.com/posts/hutt-city-council_the-bins-might-not-be-the-star-of-your-event-activity-7474642423495860224-mYip","text":"The bins might not be the star of your event, but people will definitely notice if they're missing...

When you're planning an event, there's a lot to think about. The venue, the food, the entertainment, the weather (fingers crossed for sunshine).

But don't forget about the waste.

Whether you're organising a community festival, market, sports event or large public gathering, it's important to have a plan for what happens once the coffee cups, food containers and packaging start piling up.

Event organisers are responsible for managing the waste generated at their event, including providing the right bins, signage and collection systems, and making sure waste is sorted correctly.

For larger events, a Waste Minimisation and Management Plan may also be required under Hutt City Council's Solid Waste Management and Minimisation Bylaw.

Hutt City Council works with Nonstop Solutions to support eligible event organisers with waste planning, helping to reduce unnecessary waste, improve recycling outcomes, and meet event waste requirements.

If you're in the early stages of planning, it's worth thinking about:

▪️ What waste your event is likely to create
▪️ Whether reusable serviceware or low-waste packaging could be used
▪️ Where bins and signage will be placed
▪️ How waste will be sorted and collected
▪️ What reporting may be needed afterwards

Need a hand getting started? Contact Nonstop Solutions at hello@nonstopsolutions.co.nz to discuss your event waste management needs.

Together, we can create events that are easier to manage and better for te taiao.","url":"https://www.linkedin.com/posts/hutt-city-council_the-bins-might-not-be-the-star-of-your-event-activity-7474642423495860224-mYip"},{"@context":"http://schema.org","@type":"DiscussionForumPosting","author":{"@type":"Organization","name":"Hutt City Council","url":"https://nz.linkedin.com/company/hutt-city-council"},"datePublished":"2026-06-21T23:45:04.812Z","headline":"","mainEntityOfPage":"https://www.linkedin.com/posts/hutt-city-council_were-looking-for-a-new-operator-for-the-activity-7474608361372684288-d5GC","text":"We're looking for a new operator for the Lower Hutt market!

From live music and new vendors, to fresh ideas and great energy, the new operator will have the chance to put their own stamp on an already-loved community destination.

The market will continue operating at the Riverbank carpark until relocation.

🗓️ Applications close 5pm, Monday 6 July.

Apply through the Government Electronic Tender Service (GETS): https://lnkd.in/e2Qgc2is

The award recognises local government leaders aged 35 and under who have delivered innovative projects and programmes with a positive impact on their communities. 
 
Kaanihi Butler-Hare was recognised for his leadership in strengthening relationships between iwi, Māori organisations, and central and local government agencies. As an emerging leader, he has made a significant contribution early in his career.
 
The judging panel described Butler-Hare as representing "the pinnacle of next-generation bicultural leadership" recognising his ability to combine professionalism, humility and mātauranga Māori to deliver lasting impact. 
 
As part of the award, Butler-Hare will attend the 2026 International City/County Management Association Conference in Long Beach, California where local government leaders from around the world will share ideas, insights and best practice. 
 
Ka pai Kaanihi! We are incredibly proud of you and your hard mahi. A big thank you to Taituarā — Local Government Professionals Aotearoa too.","url":"https://www.linkedin.com/posts/hutt-city-council_hutt-city-councils-tumuaki-m%C4%81ori-kaanihi-activity-7473532110016921600-BedQ"},{"@context":"http://schema.org","@type":"DiscussionForumPosting","author":{"@type":"Organization","name":"Hutt City Council","url":"https://nz.linkedin.com/company/hutt-city-council"},"datePublished":"2026-06-16T03:29:58.796Z","mainEntityOfPage":"https://www.linkedin.com/posts/hutt-city-council_looking-for-a-high-visibility-branding-opportunity-activity-7472490631924469760-yn06","text":"Looking for a high-visibility branding opportunity in Lower Hutt?

▪️ Waione Street Bridge, Seaview

See all the info at hutt.city/philippinefest","url":"https://www.linkedin.com/posts/hutt-city-council_this-morning-hutt-city-council-joined-the-activity-7471054847220510720-5AwP"},{"@context":"http://schema.org","@type":"DiscussionForumPosting","author":{"@type":"Organization","name":"Hutt City Council","url":"https://nz.linkedin.com/company/hutt-city-council"},"datePublished":"2026-06-10T23:05:29.298Z","mainEntityOfPage":"https://www.linkedin.com/posts/hutt-city-council_te-ngaengae-pool-fitness-is-set-to-make-activity-7470612131101696002-6Vre","text":"Te Ngaengae Pool + Fitness is set to make a splash with solar power, helping reduce operating costs and emissions for years to come 🏊☀️

The installation of solar panels will cost approximately $881,000 and will be funded by the underspend from the original construction, which came in under budget.

The solar panels are expected to bring three main benefits:

▪️ Lower power bills, with savings estimated at about $95,000 a year

▪️ Lower emissions, with savings estimated at about 30 tonnes of CO2 a year

▪️ Better value from a community building that will be used for many years

Council’s Neighbourhoods & Communities Director Andrea Blackshaw says the solar installation is a practical step that makes good use of money already set aside for the pool.

“Te Ngaengae Pool is one of the jewels in Lower Hutt’s crown and is well-used by residents right across the city and aquatic sports across the region, so it makes sense to make it as efficient as possible.

“Pools use a lot of power for heating, lighting and running equipment. Solar power will help reduce those costs over time, while also lowering emissions.

“The pool was designed with solar in mind, and it was always intended to add it to the facility if it could be afforded. Given the current financial challenges facing Council and community, it’s critical that we run our buildings as efficiently as possible, manage costs and support a more sustainable city.”

The final size and design of the solar system will be confirmed once Council has selected a supplier through a procurement process now underway.

Te Ngaengae Pool + Fitness opened in December 2024. It was designed with sustainability in mind and achieved a Green Star Five rating, a high standard for environmentally friendly buildings. The new solar panels will build on that strong foundation.

Installation is expected to take place between September and November 2026.

Council has already installed solar panels at the Silverstream Landfill offices.         " dir="ltr" data-test-id="main-feed-activity-card__commentary">The bins might not be the star of your event, but people will definitely notice if they're missing...

When you're planning an event, there's a lot to think about. The venue, the food, the entertainment, the weather (fingers crossed for sunshine).

But don't forget about the waste.

Whether you're organising a community festival, market, sports event or large public gathering, it's important to have a plan for what happens once the coffee cups, food containers and packaging start piling up.

Event organisers are responsible for managing the waste generated at their event, including providing the right bins, signage and collection systems, and making sure waste is sorted correctly.

For larger events, a Waste Minimisation and Management Plan may also be required under Hutt City Council's Solid Waste Management and Minimisation Bylaw.

Hutt City Council works with <a class="link" href="https://nz.linkedin.com/company/nonstop-solutionsnz?trk=organization_guest_main-feed-card-text" target="_self" data-tracking-control-name="organization_guest_main-feed-card-text" data-tracking-will-navigate>Nonstop Solutions</a> to support eligible event organisers with waste planning, helping to reduce unnecessary waste, improve recycling outcomes, and meet event waste requirements.

If you're in the early stages of planning, it's worth thinking about:

▪️ What waste your event is likely to create
▪️ Whether reusable serviceware or low-waste packaging could be used
▪️ Where bins and signage will be placed
▪️ How waste will be sorted and collected
▪️ What reporting may be needed afterwards

Need a hand getting started?         " dir="ltr" data-test-id="main-feed-activity-card__commentary">Hutt City Council's Tumuaki Māori <a class="link" href="https://nz.linkedin.com/in/kaanihi-butler-hare-b8006a259?trk=organization_guest_main-feed-card-text" target="_self" data-tracking-control-name="organization_guest_main-feed-card-text" data-tracking-will-navigate>Kaanihi Butler-Hare</a> has received the 2026 Sheffield Emerging Leader of the Year Award presented at the LGFA Taituarā Local Government Excellence Awards held in Wellington last night. 
 
The award recognises local government leaders aged 35 and under who have delivered innovative projects and programmes with a positive impact on their communities. 
 
Kaanihi Butler-Hare was recognised for his leadership in strengthening relationships between iwi, Māori organisations, and central and local government agencies. As an emerging leader, he has made a significant contribution early in his career.
 
The judging panel described Butler-Hare as representing "the pinnacle of next-generation bicultural leadership" recognising his ability to combine professionalism, humility and mātauranga Māori to deliver lasting impact. 
 
As part of the award, Butler-Hare will attend the 2026 International City/County Management Association Conference in Long Beach, California where local government leaders from around the world will share ideas, insights and best practice. 
 
Ka pai Kaanihi! We are incredibly proud of you and your hard mahi. A big thank you to <a class="link" href="https://nz.linkedin.com/company/taituara?trk=organization_guest_main-feed-card-text" target="_self" data-tracking-control-name="organization_guest_main-feed-card-text" data-tracking-will-navigate>Taituarā — Local Government Professionals Aotearoa</a> too.</p>

    <p class="attributed-text-segment-list__content text-color-text !text-sm whitespace-pre-wrap break-words
        " dir="ltr" data-test-id="main-feed-activity-card__commentary">Te Ngaengae Pool + Fitness is set to make a splash with solar power, helping reduce operating costs and emissions for years to come 🏊☀️

The installation of solar panels will cost approximately $881,000 and will be funded by the underspend from the original construction, which came in under budget.

The solar panels are expected to bring three main benefits:

▪️ Lower power bills, with savings estimated at about $95,000 a year

▪️ Lower emissions, with savings estimated at about 30 tonnes of CO2 a year

▪️ Better value from a community building that will be used for many years

Council’s Neighbourhoods & Communities Director Andrea Blackshaw says the solar installation is a practical step that makes good use of money already set aside for the pool.

“Te Ngaengae Pool is one of the jewels in Lower Hutt’s crown and is well-used by residents right across the city and aquatic sports across the region, so it makes sense to make it as efficient as possible.

“Pools use a lot of power for heating, lighting and running equipment. Solar power will help reduce those costs over time, while also lowering emissions.

“The pool was designed with solar in mind, and it was always intended to add it to the facility if it could be afforded. Given the current financial challenges facing Council and community, it’s critical that we run our buildings as efficiently as possible, manage costs and support a more sustainable city.”

The final size and design of the solar system will be confirmed once Council has selected a supplier through a procurement process now underway.

Te Ngaengae Pool + Fitness opened in December 2024. It was designed with sustainability in mind and achieved a Green Star Five rating, a high standard for environmentally friendly buildings. The new solar panels will build on that strong foundation.

Installation is expected to take place between September and November 2026.

Council has already installed solar panels at the Silverstream Landfill offices. Te Ngaengae Pool + Fitness will be its first large solar project.</p>
